How it works

An air fryer is a small convection oven: a fan blows hot air around food in a small space, so it browns and cooks faster than a regular oven. The usual rule is to set it 25 °F lower (about 15 °C) and cut the time by about 20%. The converter rounds the time to the nearest whole minute and never goes below 1 minute.

Going the other way, from an air fryer recipe to the oven, it adds 25 °F back and adds about 25% to the time, which undoes the 20% cut. It all runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere or saved.

Ways to use it

  • Baked recipes. Cookies, muffins and small bakes, in batches that fit the basket.
  • Frozen foods. Fries, nuggets and pizza rolls: take the oven time on the bag and convert it.
  • Leftovers. Reheating pizza or fried chicken gets it crisp instead of soggy.
  • Roasted vegetables. Spread them in one layer so the air can get around them.
  • Chicken and fries. Check chicken with a thermometer (165 °F) rather than trusting the time.

Questions

Why is the air fryer temperature lower?

The fan moves hot air right across the food in a small space, so the outside browns faster than in a regular oven. Lowering the temperature by 25 °F gives the middle time to cook before the outside burns.

How much shorter is the time?

About 20% shorter. A 20-minute oven recipe takes about 16 minutes, and a 30-minute one about 24. Start checking a few minutes before that the first time, because air fryers vary.

Do I still preheat?

Most air fryers heat up in 2 to 3 minutes. Preheat if your manual says to, or add a couple of minutes to the time if you start cold.

What if my air fryer only shows Celsius?

Switch the converter to °C. It takes off 15 °C, so a 200 °C oven recipe becomes 185 °C in the air fryer.

Is anything saved?

No. The converter runs in your browser, and nothing you type is sent anywhere or saved.
